analysis.investment_thesis: Aaradhya Disposal trades at a P/E of 12.4 yet delivers a miserable 0.45% ROE — this is a low-quality microcap where the optically low multiple reflects near-zero earning power, not a bargain. Without multi-year audited earnings history, adequate returns on capital, or a demonstrated dividend record, it fails my core quantitative tests.
key_strengths: P/E of 12.4 is below my 15x ceiling
key_risks: ROE of 0.45% signals virtually no real earning power
Microcap (INR 159 Cr) with limited liquidity and disclosure depth
No visible dividend history or balance-sheet data (D/E, current ratio unknown)
red_flags: Insufficient data on debt, current ratio, book value for Graham Number
Commodity-exposed paper industry with thin margins
Recent listing profile typical of speculative SME issuance
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Graham lens, the single most damning figure is the 0.45% ROE. A P/E of 12.4 only looks cheap until you realize earnings are a rounding error on equity — at that return, shareholders would be better off in a savings account. I cannot compute the Graham Number without book value and EPS, but any business earning sub-1% on equity cannot generate the proven earning power I require. The 70.58% promoter stake is reassuring for alignment but also means minimal public float and governance scrutiny.

The absence of disclosed current ratio, debt-to-equity, interest coverage, and dividend history means the company fails my documentation bar before it even fails my numerical ones. Paper products is a commodity industry with input-cost volatility, and a 12-year-old microcap in this space offers no durable moat. Mr. Market is not offering a bargain here — he is offering a mediocre business at a mediocre price. Pass.
